questions.text: A solid hemisphere of radius 14 cm is cut by a plane through its axis, perpendicular to its flat base, into two equal parts. Taking π = 22/7, what is the total surface area of one part?
questions.explanation: One part has three surfaces: curved surface = ½ × 2πr² = πr² = 616; half of the flat base = ½πr² = 308; and the new cut face, a semicircle of radius 14, = ½πr² = 308. Total = 616 + 308 + 308 = 1,232 cm² (= 2πr²).
steps: Half of the flat base: ½πr² = 308
Cut face is a semicircle: ½πr² = 308
questions.trap: Halving 3πr² forgets that cutting creates a new face.
wrongReasons: Halved the hemisphere's total surface area (3πr²) instead of adding the new cut face
Gave the total surface area of the whole hemisphere
Counted only the curved surface of the part
questions.shortcut: Every cut through a solid adds two new faces in total, one to each piece: count the cut face.

questions.text: The base of a right prism is a rhombus whose diagonals are 24 cm and 18 cm. If the volume of the prism is 3,240 cm³, what is its total surface area?
questions.explanation: Side of the rhombus = √(12² + 9²) = 15 cm, perimeter 60. Base area = ½ × 24 × 18 = 216. Height = 3,240 ÷ 216 = 15 cm. TSA = 60 × 15 + 2 × 216 = 900 + 432 = 1,332 cm².
questions.trap: Using d₁ × d₂ as the rhombus area.
questions.revise: Prism: base area, height from volume, TSA
wrongReasons: Gave only the lateral surface area
Added only one base to the lateral surface
Took the base area as 24 × 18 without the half

questions.text: A conical vessel with base radius 12 cm and height 35 cm is full of water. Its contents are poured 15 times into an empty cylindrical tank of base radius 20 cm, refilling the cone each time. What is the height of water in the tank?
questions.explanation: Volume of the cone = ⅓π × 12² × 35 = 1,680π. Fifteen cones = 25,200π. Base of the tank = π × 20² = 400π, so the height = 25,200 ÷ 400 = 63 cm.
questions.trap: Forgetting the ⅓ or mixing radius and diameter.
wrongReasons: Gave the rise after a single emptying
Left out the ⅓ in the cone's volume
Used the tank's diameter (40 cm) as its radius

questions.text: A bucket is in the form of a frustum of a cone with top and bottom radii 21 cm and 7 cm and a slant height of 50 cm. Taking π = 22/7, what is its capacity in litres?
questions.explanation: The vertical height is h = √(50² − (21 − 7)²) = √(2,500 − 196) = 48 cm. Volume = ⅓πh(R² + Rr + r²) = ⅓ × 22/7 × 48 × (441 + 147 + 49) = 32,032 cm³ = 32.032 litres.
questions.trap: Using the slant height in the volume formula.
questions.revise: Frustum: slant height vs vertical height
wrongReasons: Used the slant height 50 cm as the vertical height
Left out the product of the two radii (Rr) term
Left out the ⅓ in the frustum formula

questions.text: The perimeter of a semicircular park, including its diameter, is 72 m. Taking π = 22/7, what is the area of the park?
questions.explanation: Perimeter = πr + 2r = r(22/7 + 2) = 36r/7 = 72, so r = 14 m. Area = ½πr² = ½ × 22/7 × 196 = 308 m².
questions.trap: Forgetting that the diameter is part of the perimeter.
questions.revise: Perimeter and area of a semicircle
wrongReasons: Gave the area of the full circle
Gave the area of a quarter circle
Took the area of the enclosing rectangle 28 × 14

questions.text: A solid metal sphere of radius 9 cm is melted and recast into small cones, each of base radius 3 cm and height 4.5 cm. If 25% of the metal is lost in the process, how many cones can be made?
questions.explanation: Sphere volume = 4/3 π × 729 = 972π. Usable metal = 0.75 × 972π = 729π. One cone = ⅓π × 9 × 4.5 = 13.5π. Number = 729 ÷ 13.5 = 54.
questions.trap: Applying the loss in the wrong direction.
wrongReasons: Ignored the 25% loss
Divided by 0.75 instead of multiplying
Left out the ⅓ in the cone's volume

questions.text: The areas of three adjacent faces of a cuboid are 60 cm², 72 cm² and 120 cm². What is the sum of the lengths of all its 12 edges?
questions.explanation: If the edges are a, b, c then ab = 60, bc = 72, ca = 120, so (abc)² = 60 × 72 × 120 = 518,400 and abc = 720. So c = 720 ÷ 60 = 12, a = 720 ÷ 72 = 10, b = 720 ÷ 120 = 6. Total length of edges = 4(a + b + c) = 4 × 28 = 112 cm.
questions.trap: Stopping at a + b + c or forgetting that each edge occurs four times.
wrongReasons: Gave a + b + c, the sum of the three different edges
Gave the perimeter-like 2(a + b + c)
Added the three face areas

questions.text: The mean of 12 numbers is 40. Each of the first 5 numbers is increased by 7 and each of the remaining 7 numbers is decreased by 5. What is the new mean?
questions.explanation: Total change = 5 × 7 − 7 × 5 = 35 − 35 = 0, so the sum, and therefore the mean, is unchanged at 40.
questions.trap: Averaging the changes without weighting them by how many numbers each applies to.
wrongReasons: Averaged the two changes (+7 and −5)
Added the net change of 2 straight to the mean
Averaged the two changes and subtracted it

questions.text: The mean of the following distribution is 36. Find the missing frequency x.
questions.trap: Using class limits instead of class marks.
questions.revise: Mean of grouped data with an unknown frequency
wrongReasons: Gives a mean of about 36.14
Gives a mean of about 36.08
Gives a mean of about 35.89

questions.text: Find the median of the following frequency distribution.
questions.explanation: N = 56, so N/2 = 28. Cumulative frequencies: 5, 13, 25, 40, 50, 56. The median class is 40–50 with cf before = 25 and f = 15. Median = 40 + (28 − 25)/15 × 10 = 42.
questions.trap: Choosing the median class by looking at N rather than N/2.
wrongReasons: Used the class 30–40 with the wrong cumulative frequency
Forgot to multiply by the class width
Took the mid-point of the median class

questions.text: In a class of 45 students the average marks of the boys are 72 and of the girls 81. If the average of the whole class is 75, how many girls are there?
questions.trap: Writing the ratio the wrong way round.
wrongReasons: Gave the number of boys
Split the class (about) equally
Read the boys : girls ratio as 3 : 2
questions.shortcut: Boys : girls is the gap on the girls' side to the gap on the boys' side.

questions.text: For a moderately skewed distribution the mean is 24 and the median is 22. What is the approximate value of the mode?
questions.explanation: Mode ≈ 3 × median − 2 × mean = 66 − 48 = 18.
questions.trap: Reversing the empirical formula.
wrongReasons: Swapped the mean and the median in the formula
Took the average of the mean and the median
Took the median as the mode

questions.text: The standard deviation of 5 observations is 6. Each observation is multiplied by 3 and then 4 is added. What is the variance of the new set?
questions.explanation: Adding 4 does not change spread; multiplying by 3 multiplies the SD by 3: new SD = 18. Variance = 18² = 324.
steps: Shift of +4: no change in spread
questions.trap: Adding the shift to the SD, or answering with the SD.
questions.revise: SD under change of origin and scale
wrongReasons: Gave the original variance
Treated 6 × 3 + 4 as the SD, not the variance
Gave the new standard deviation only

questions.text: ₹ 8,000 is invested for 1½ years at 10% per annum. What is the difference between the amount when interest is compounded half-yearly and the amount when it is compounded annually (simple interest being taken for the half year)?
questions.explanation: Half-yearly: 8,000 × 1.05³ = 9,261. Annual compounding for 1 year gives 8,800, and the last half-year earns simple interest of 5% on 8,800 = 440, so the amount is 9,240. Difference = 9,261 − 9,240 = ₹ 21.
questions.trap: Using the half-yearly rule for the annual case, or a fractional exponent.
wrongReasons: Used the exact fractional power 1.1^1.5 for the annual case
Compared the first year only
Compared with simple interest instead of annual compounding

questions.text: A and B start a business with ₹ 30,000 and ₹ 60,000. After 5 months A withdraws one-third of his capital, and after 8 months C joins with ₹ 60,000. At the end of the year the total profit is ₹ 1,05,000. What is C's share (in ₹)?
questions.trap: Using capital ratio only, or forgetting that A's capital changes after 5 months.
wrongReasons: Ignored the time for which each amount was invested
Ignored A's withdrawal
Used 24 parts out of 100 instead of out of 125

questions.text: A, B and C can complete a piece of work in 24, 36 and 72 days respectively. A and B begin together. After 8 days A leaves and C joins B. After 6 more days B also leaves and the remaining work is finished by C alone. In how many days in all is the work completed?
questions.explanation: Per day: A = 3/72, B = 2/72, C = 1/72. First 8 days: 8 × 5/72 = 40/72. Next 6 days (B + C): 6 × 3/72 = 18/72. Done = 58/72, left = 14/72, which C does in 14 days. Total = 8 + 6 + 14 = 28 days.
steps: Remaining 72 − 58 = 14, done by C in 14 days
questions.trap: Dropping a stage or using the wrong pair of workers.
questions.revise: Time and work with changing workers
wrongReasons: Gave only C's final stretch
Forgot the 6-day middle stage
Let B work alone in the second stage, forgetting that C had joined
questions.shortcut: Take the LCM (72) as the total work so every rate is a whole number.

questions.text: A boat takes 12 hours to cover 36 km upstream and 54 km downstream, and 13 hours to cover 54 km upstream and 36 km downstream. What is the speed of the stream (in km/h)?
questions.explanation: Let 1/u = x and 1/d = y. Then 36x + 54y = 12 and 54x + 36y = 13. Solving gives x = 1/6 and y = 1/9, so upstream speed = 6 and downstream speed = 9 km/h. Stream speed = (9 − 6)/2 = 1.5 km/h.
questions.trap: Quoting the still-water speed or forgetting to halve.
questions.revise: Upstream and downstream with two equations
wrongReasons: Gave the difference of the two speeds without halving
Gave the speed in still water
Added the upstream and downstream speeds

questions.text: A vessel contains 60 litres of pure milk. 12 litres are taken out and replaced by water. Then 15 litres of the mixture are taken out and replaced by water. What is the ratio of milk to water in the vessel now?
questions.explanation: After the first step: milk 48, water 12. The 15 litres removed contain 15 × 48/60 = 12 litres of milk, so milk = 36 and water = 24. Ratio = 36 : 24 = 3 : 2.
steps: 15 L of mixture holds 12 L milk
questions.trap: Treating the second withdrawal as pure milk.
wrongReasons: Subtracted both withdrawals as if they were pure milk
Gave the ratio after the first replacement only
Used 12 litres again in the second step

questions.text: In triangle ABC, ∠A = 70°. I is the incentre and O is the circumcentre. What is the ratio ∠BIC : ∠BOC?
questions.trap: Mixing the incentre and circumcentre formulae.
wrongReasons: Used ∠BIC = 90° + ∠A instead of 90° + ½∠A
Used ∠BIC = 180° − ½∠A
Took ∠BOC as ∠A instead of 2∠A

questions.text: Two circles of radii 17 cm and 10 cm intersect, and their common chord is 16 cm long. If the centres lie on opposite sides of the common chord, what is the distance between the centres?
questions.explanation: Half the chord = 8. Distance of the centre of the bigger circle from the chord = √(17² − 8²) = 15; of the smaller = √(10² − 8²) = 6. Opposite sides: 15 + 6 = 21 cm.
questions.trap: Using the radii directly or adding when they should subtract.
wrongReasons: Gave the distance when the centres lie on the same side
Added the two radii
Added the larger radius and half of the chord

questions.text: A point P is 25 cm from the centre O of a circle of radius 7 cm. The tangents PA and PB touch the circle at A and B. What is the length of the chord AB?
questions.explanation: Tangent PA = √(25² − 7²) = 24. In the right triangle OAP, the foot of the perpendicular from A on OP gives half the chord = (OA × PA)/OP = 7 × 24/25 = 6.72. So AB = 2 × 6.72 = 13.44 cm.
questions.trap: Stopping at the tangent length.
wrongReasons: Gave the length of a tangent
Gave the diameter
Gave half of the chord

questions.text: In trapezium ABCD, AB ∥ CD and AB = 2 × CD. The diagonals meet at O. If the area of triangle AOB is 72 cm², what is the area of the trapezium?
questions.explanation: Triangles AOB and COD are similar with ratio 2 : 1, so area COD = 72 ÷ 4 = 18. The side triangles AOD and BOC have equal areas √(72 × 18) = 36 each. Total = 72 + 18 + 36 + 36 = 162 cm².
questions.trap: Forgetting the two side triangles.
wrongReasons: Added only triangles AOB and COD
Counted only one of the two side triangles
Took three times the area of AOB

questions.text: If sec θ + tan θ = 3 and θ is acute, what is the value of cosec θ + cot θ?
questions.explanation: sec θ − tan θ = 1/3, so sec θ = (3 + 1/3)/2 = 5/3 and tan θ = 4/3. Then cos θ = 3/5 and sin θ = 4/5, so cosec θ + cot θ = 5/4 + 3/4 = 2.
questions.trap: Swapping sine and cosine.
wrongReasons: Swapped sin θ and cos θ
Gave cosec θ only
Gave cot θ only

questions.text: From the top of a 60 m tower, the angles of depression of two points on the same side of the tower and in line with its foot are 30° and 60°. What is the distance between the two points?
questions.explanation: Farther point: 60 ÷ tan 30° = 60√3. Nearer point: 60 ÷ tan 60° = 20√3. Distance between them = 60√3 − 20√3 = 40√3 m.
questions.trap: Using the sum when both points are on the same side.
wrongReasons: Gave the distance of the nearer point from the foot
Gave the distance of the farther point from the foot
Added the two distances, as for points on opposite sides

questions.text: What is the value of tan² 15° + cot² 15°?
questions.explanation: tan 15° = 2 − √3 and cot 15° = 2 + √3, so tan 15° + cot 15° = 4. Then tan² + cot² = (tan + cot)² − 2 tan cot = 16 − 2 = 14.
questions.trap: Forgetting the −2 term.
wrongReasons: Squared tan 15° + cot 15° and did not subtract 2
Gave tan 15° + cot 15° without squaring
Evaluated (cot 15° − tan 15°)²

questions.text: If a + b + c = 12 and ab + bc + ca = 47, what is the value of a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc?
questions.explanation: a² + b² + c² = 12² − 2 × 47 = 50. The expression = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca) = 12 × (50 − 47) = 36.
questions.trap: Forgetting the factor 2 in (a + b + c)².
wrongReasons: Gave only the second factor of the identity
Used a² + b² + c² = 144 − 47 instead of 144 − 94
Gave a² + b² + c² only

questions.text: If x² − 6x + 1 = 0, what is the value of x⁴ + 1/x⁴?
questions.explanation: Divide by x: x + 1/x = 6. Then x² + 1/x² = 36 − 2 = 34 and x⁴ + 1/x⁴ = 34² − 2 = 1,154.
questions.trap: Stopping early or forgetting to subtract 2 twice.
wrongReasons: Gave x² + 1/x²
Forgot to subtract 2 in the last step
Subtracted 4 instead of 2

questions.text: The sum of the digits of a two-digit number is 11. If 27 is subtracted from the number, the digits are reversed. What is the number?
questions.explanation: Let the number be 10a + b. a + b = 11 and (10a + b) − (10b + a) = 27 gives a − b = 3. So a = 7 and b = 4: the number is 74.
questions.trap: Choosing a number only from the digit sum.
wrongReasons: Gave the reversed number
Digits sum to 11 but 83 − 27 = 56
Digits sum to 11 but 92 − 27 = 65

questions.text: How many integers from 1 to 200 are divisible by 3 or 5 but not by 15?
questions.explanation: Multiples of 3: 66; of 5: 40; of 15: 13. Divisible by 3 or 5 = 66 + 40 − 13 = 93. Remove those divisible by 15: 93 − 13 = 80. (Equivalently 66 + 40 − 2 × 13.)
questions.trap: Using inclusion–exclusion but forgetting the 'not by 15' condition.
wrongReasons: Did not exclude the multiples of 15
Added the multiples of 3 and 5 without removing the common ones
Removed the multiples of 15 twice from 93 and then added again

questions.text: What is the value of √0.0081 × ∛0.000343 ÷ 0.21?
questions.trap: Decimal-place slips when taking roots.
wrongReasons: Misplaced the decimal point by one place
Misplaced the decimal point by one place the other way
Gave only √0.0081
